gabriel-buelna.text: Says he wants the board to focus on support services that help students overcome barriers, and on academic standards so students finish with a degree or certificate that prepares them for further schooling or a good job.

source.title: Buelna for College Board 2026 - A Message from Dr. Buelna

gabriel-buelna.text: Says community colleges "should be engines of economic opportunity and success" and recalls that LACCD courses helped his immigrant parents become citizens.

source.title: Buelna for College Board 2026 - A Message from Dr. Buelna

gabriel-buelna.text: Endorsed by the LA/OC Building Trades Council, SEIU Local 99, AFT College Staff Guild 1521A, the CSUN chapter of the California Faculty Association, Teamsters Joint Council 42, IUOE Local 12, UFCW 770 and other trade unions.
Endorsed by the California Democratic Renters Council.
Endorsed by Rep. Judy Chu, Rep. Luz Rivas, Treasurer Fiona Ma, Assemblymember Mike Fong, and former Mayor Eric Garcetti.

randall-winston.text: Pledges to accelerate affordable student housing, noting 70% of LACCD students face housing insecurity and citing his past direction of $1.3 billion in investments through the California Strategic Growth Council.
Pledges to expand support services and financial aid that keep students enrolled, focusing on veterans, first-generation, low-income and working students.
Pledges to strengthen partnerships with labor and industry so students move directly into good-paying, high-demand careers.
Pledges to "protect LACCD's mission" of accessible, high-quality education for every student.
Endorsed by the LA County Federation of Labor, AFT College Guild 1521, AFT Staff Guild 1521A, SEIU 721, IBEW 11, SMART Local 105 and UTLA.
Endorsed by the Los Angeles County Democratic Party; his site also lists Mayor Karen Bass and former Gov. Jerry Brown.

notes: No LACCD campaign positions found for tonia-arey (a Realtor who also ran for LA County Supervisor District 3; her campaign site was no longer a live campaign page) or roberto-david-lacarra (search found a Roberto LaCarra running for State Senate District 20, but nothing fetched ties it to this LACCD race, so nothing was recorded). Buelna's site gives few concrete policy positions; LACCD trustee pages were blocked (403), so no board voting record was retrieved.
